answer.rationale: Constraints prune most of the candidate set before memory even matters. Rollback is off the table by compliance ruling, so memory_b1 (the strongest-looking precedent) is unusable and not worth a verification pull. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) succeeded by failing fast on a dependency, but here the degraded path IS the write path at settlement peak — failing fast would shed exactly the customer writes the objective forbids losing. Regional failover (memory_b2) succeeded during a read/latency degradation; cutting over a write-heavy primary at daily peak risks in-flight write loss and is the highest-variance option. Add capacity (memory_b3) worked when provisioned BEFORE a known surge; provisioning mid-incident is unlikely to land inside the 90-minute degradation curve. That leaves route_read_replicas, and memory_b5 is the one memory whose recorded outcome maps onto the actual symptom: offloading report/dashboard reads relieved contention and transactional write latency recovered same-day. That is why I spend the single verification pull on b5 rather than on the more famous-looking b1. What I need from the archive is whether b5's causal story holds: was the primary's write latency actually driven by report-query contention, or did b5 coincide with an unrelated fix? If the original record shows the win was incidental, read-routing becomes a no-op here and I would fall back to add_capacity as the least write-endangering option. Uncertainty that survives regardless: none of the six memories were recorded under simultaneous peak-write load plus a non-revertible release, so all of them are being extrapolated past their original conditions, and the release two hours ago remains an unexcluded cause of the climb that I cannot test by reverting. Downstream value risk: shifting reads to replicas introduces replication lag into reconciliation, settlement reporting, and any fraud or limit checks that read those paths — stale reads at settlement peak can produce wrong balances and duplicate-payout decisions that look like success on the latency dashboard while corrupting financial state. So I gate it: start with clearly non-authoritative report/dashboard query classes only, exclude anything feeding settlement or authorization decisions, watch replica lag alongside p99, and expand only if lag stays bounded. Small guarded test rather than broad rollout because it is cheaply reversible and the staleness blast radius is the real hazard, not the latency.
